name: Jellyfin
description: Media server for your own movies, shows, and music.
about: Organizes your movies, shows, music, and photos and streams them to browsers, phones, TVs, and set top boxes. The first start opens a setup wizard where you create the admin account and add your libraries. Apps will not find this server by themselves, because the discovery broadcast does not cross a container network. Give them the server's address instead.

variables.label: Media folder
variables.description: Media folder mounted at /media, the path to select when adding libraries.

variables.label: Config folder
variables.description: The database, downloaded metadata images, plugins, and logs. This is the folder to back up.

variables.label: Cache folder
variables.description: Temporary transcoding files and cached images. Use a different folder from the config folder or startup fails.

variables.label: Web UI port
variables.description: Host port for the web UI and client API.

variables.label: Published server URL
variables.description: URL reported in UDP discovery responses. This template does not publish the discovery port, so enter the server address in your clients.

variables.label: HTTPS port
variables.description: Publishes 8920, the container's HTTPS port. Nothing answers there until you add a certificate under Dashboard, Networking. Blank publishes nothing.

variables.label: GPU device
variables.description: Host device passed through for VAAPI or QSV transcoding, usually /dev/dri. Blank leaves transcoding on the CPU. NVIDIA needs the container toolkit runtime, which a template cannot set.

variables.label: Run as user
variables.description: Numeric uid:gid. Blank runs the server as root, which is what the image does. It needs read access to the media folder, and a gid that can read the GPU device if you passed one through.

variables.label: Timezone
variables.description: IANA name such as Europe/London. Sets the container's local time, which log timestamps and daily scheduled tasks use.
